idiom_name: dlopen plus a @_cdecl entry point returning an opaque plugin object
implementation_notes: Swift has no supported way to load Swift types out of a plugin library - a plugin module carries its own copy of the contract types, so the runtime sees two nominal types and the plugin's conformances do not match the host's - so the community mechanism is the C ABI: the plugin exports an entry point with @_cdecl and returns an opaque pointer (or a @convention(c) function table), and the host resolves it with dlopen/dlsym and wraps it with Unmanaged. On Apple platforms the Objective-C runtime path (Bundle/NSBundle and the runtime's dynamic discovery) can load concrete classes without dlsym, but there is still no Swift-native registry, and SwiftPM's build tool and command plugins are build-time extensions, not runtime plugins. Everything else - discovery of the plugin directory, version checks, lifecycle and isolation - is hand-written, which is why the pattern is usually implemented by hosting the extension in a separate process instead.
pitfalls: dlsym cannot turn an arbitrary symbol address into a Swift function value (calling conventions differ); only @convention(c) entry points are safe, and the C ABI must carry every value that crosses.

Swift is not ABI stable outside the OS-shipped runtime (the Replaceable Library Plugins pitch notes this for Linux), so host and plugins must be built with the same compiler and runtime, and mixing dependencies into a plugin has caused intermittent crashes in practice.

Unloading is effectively unsupported: dlclose with Swift runtime metadata and retained class registrations in play is unsafe, and RTLD_NODELETE is the usual workaround, which leaks the library by design.
